title: Completion made reflection symmetry portable without solving zero location
claim: The historical move from Riemann's contour-derived completed zeta expression to the centered xi function and then to completed L-functions standardized a representation in which s and 1-s are directly comparable. That standardization isolates trivial factors and makes symmetry portable across families, but it also exposes a persistent obstruction: reflection symmetry organizes zeros without forcing them onto the symmetry line.
historical_or_program_relation: Riemann's completion mechanism became a family-wide analytic interface; later accounts sharpen the distinction between achieving the interface and discharging the zero-location burden.
limits: The indexed units do not claim that all completions arise by the same derivation, identify the completed functions with one another, or show that functional equations are irrelevant to an eventual proof.

title: Prime smoothing evolved as a reversible or deliberately lossy analytic interface
claim: Across the historical prime-counting line, prime powers and logarithmic weights replace raw prime indicators because multiplicative products then become additive sums accessible to complex analysis and combinatorial bounds. Riemann's squarefree alternating inversion shows that one such smoothing retains exact recoverability, while later weighted-count and von Mangoldt representations intentionally trade itemwise locations for tractable aggregate control.
historical_or_program_relation: The program progresses from an exact prime-power smoothing/inversion pair to choosing weighted observables according to the algebra and estimates they enable, making information loss an audited design choice rather than an accidental byproduct.
limits: Exact recoverability for Riemann's specific transform does not transfer automatically to every later weighting; the Bombieri and Moree units do not by themselves supply an RH proof or a uniform error term for ordinary prime counts.

title: Finite RH computation became local detection plus independent completeness accounting
claim: The computational line develops a stable certificate architecture: a real critical-line representation makes sign changes cheap local witnesses, remainder-aware abstention and refinement protect those witnesses, and an argument-principle or Turing-style total independently accounts for every zero in the bounded region. Later implementations recognize that sign events, rather than high-precision zero coordinates, are the sufficient local statistic once the global count closes the completeness gap.
historical_or_program_relation: The 1956 Riemann-Siegel sign computations are refined in later expositions into an explicit two-channel protocol and, by 2021, a goal-directed compression of what the computation must retain.
limits: This architecture certifies only the stated finite window and depends on rigorous error and contour/count hypotheses; finding many apparent line zeros without the independent total is not the same certificate.

title: Finite agreement becomes global evidence only through a separate stability theorem
claim: Finite computation can be exact about a bounded universal claim while remaining silent about the unbounded tail. The obstruction is not merely insufficient scale: extremely slow divergence can mimic bounded behavior, and even striking agreement of finite-prime approximants with a target requires compact-uniform convergence and a zero-stability theorem such as Hurwitz before line-supported finite zeros can constrain a global limit.
historical_or_program_relation: Modern certified-height work clarifies the epistemic boundary already implicit in computational history, while the proposed finite-prime program names the additional analytic bridge that extrapolation would have to supply.
limits: The convergence-and-Hurwitz bridge belongs to the specific approximating family in the Connes unit, not to every computation; conversely, this limitation does not weaken the exact finite claim certified below a verified height.

title: Finite-field success turned the classical analogy into a checklist of missing structures
claim: The positive-characteristic history decomposes a geometric RH route into algebraized correspondences, their action on differentials, a norm, and positivity, sharply separating achieved construction from missing proof steps. Classical RH surveys recast the gap as absent cohomology, Frobenius, and index-pairing roles, while the Scaling Site program proposes a geometry in which adelic scaling is read as Frobenius. The analogy becomes useful only when it specifies which structural jobs remain unfilled.
historical_or_program_relation: A successful avatar of RH changes the classical program from imitating finite-field vocabulary to seeking functional replacements for the operator, state space, and positive pairing that made the avatar tractable.
limits: The Scaling Site relation does not establish a classical cohomology theory or transfer positivity, and Hasse's incomplete correspondence program is not the same construction as the later adelic proposal.

title: Semi-local trace formulas isolate positivity while exposing the missing global normalization
claim: Weil's test-function interface converts zero location into positivity inequalities coupling primes, zeros, and archimedean data. Semi-localization makes the relevant quotient, scaling action, trace identity, and support-restricted test functions controllable, suggesting a positive-operator factorization; yet it simultaneously loses the global Poisson relation that fixes local principal values. Even a Hilbert-space identification of the semilocal quotient supplies an interface, not the required positive pairing.
historical_or_program_relation: The program refines a global positivity criterion into finite-place operator obligations, thereby localizing both the prospective construction and the normalization defect rather than claiming that spectral language alone resolves RH.
limits: The cited positive operator is a proposed or failed route, the support-restricted statement retains vanishing-moment hypotheses, and the semilocal module identification is explicitly not a positivity result.

title: Random-matrix statistics progressed from analogy to a one-way obstruction test
claim: Unfolded zero spacings and GUE statistics reveal stable local interaction laws while discarding absolute height and global arithmetic variation, which obstructs reading the comparison as a fixed global spectral operator. Nevertheless, zero-spacing statistics can become rigorous downstream input: Rodgers and Tao use a positive density of small gaps to falsify the excessive gap concentration forced by a separate near-equilibrium energy hypothesis.
historical_or_program_relation: The random-matrix viewpoint moves from classifying local statistics and generating predictions to serving as an independent contradiction channel against a dynamical model, without becoming a pointwise identification of zeta zeros with matrix eigenvalues.
limits: Local GUE agreement neither places real parts of zeros nor constructs a Hilbert-Polya operator; the Rodgers-Tao use depends on its own heat-flow and renormalized-energy argument, not on the analogy alone.

title: De Bruijn-Newman lower bounds shifted from polynomial witnesses to collective zero dynamics
claim: The deformation threshold turns a universal real-zero question into the search for an obstruction below a parameter. Early work certified a nonreal exact polynomial root from approximate coefficients; Lehmer-pair work compressed a close pair and its inverse-square environment into a robust scalar lower bound; the later dynamical argument renormalized the whole near-equilibrium configuration and contradicted its statistical consequence. Each stage enlarges the certificate from one auxiliary polynomial, to one interacting pair, to a population-level energy obstruction.
historical_or_program_relation: This is a change in witness scale within one threshold program: improved lower bounds came from progressively more structural representations of how zeros can fail to remain real under backward heat flow.
limits: The certificate types are not equivalent or interchangeable, the Lehmer-pair route requires environmental control and does not supply an infinite family, and the early finite computations do not contain the later global contradiction.

title: Lower and upper Newman bounds consume fundamentally different finite evidence
claim: A certified Lehmer pair maps local gap-and-environment data to a lower bound on the de Bruijn-Newman threshold, whereas a sufficiently high finite RH verification maps a universal bounded zero-location certificate to an improved upper bound only after a published height threshold is crossed. The two channels can bracket the same scalar but compress different information and have different limiting logic.
historical_or_program_relation: The historical lower-bound search and the later verified-height transfer are complementary sides of the deformation program, not repeated measurements of one phenomenon.
limits: One pair need not force a nonnegative threshold, extra verified height may have no stated effect before the cutoff, and neither channel by itself identifies the threshold with zero or proves RH.

title: Close-zero anomalies changed from detection hazards into scale-normalized certificates
claim: The 1956 computation separated the rising frequency of Gram-law failures from their nearly balanced displacement direction and traced difficult intervals to low-amplitude extrema between close roots. Later Lehmer-pair work stopped treating a tiny gap alone as meaningful: it normalized that gap against interaction from all other zeros, then showed that the squared gap controls the scale of a certified deformation bound. A computational nuisance became useful only after conditioning and environment were represented explicitly.
historical_or_program_relation: Historical root-finding anomalies supplied the local geometry that later threshold work converted into dimensionless, globally audited witnesses.
limits: Not every Gram failure or close pair is a Lehmer pair, the 1956 trend does not imply a deformation result, and environmental certification remains necessary even when the leading gap term is dominant.

title: Equivalent RH criteria differ sharply in proof visibility and failure modes
claim: Logical equivalence can compress RH into determinant growth, Möbius cancellation, cyclotomic boundary height, or growth of an entire series without exposing a controllable intermediate mechanism. The historical Mertens obstruction adds a second warning: strengthening an equivalent asymptotic into a sharper pointwise assertion can introduce false rigidity, while omitted quantifiers can make an advertised specialization unsafe.
historical_or_program_relation: The proliferation of criteria shifts a central research task from discovering more equivalents to auditing which representation preserves the obstruction, supplies usable intermediate observables, and states the exact quantifiers needed for the return map to RH.
limits: The evidence does not show that the named criteria are permanently infertile, equate their analytic mechanisms, or invalidate the correctly quantified RH-equivalent statements.

title: Physical and spectral reframings repeatedly fail when phase information is discarded
claim: Several RH-motivated physical representations expose the same audit principle: unsigned phase-space area can miss the absorption sign retained by Maslov phases, principal arguments require zero-dependent jump corrections, and ordinary Wigner overlap loses relational complex phase that a cross-state operator restores. Apparent single-system synthesis can also hide a conjugate component in boundary-conditioned initialization.
historical_or_program_relation: As spectral and scattering analogies became more concrete, the obstruction moved from finding a suggestive observable to proving that the representation preserves sign, branch, and relational-phase data through every transformation.
limits: These are distinct constructions with no established common operator or transfer theorem; the shared information-loss diagnosis does not validate any physical model of zeta zeros or prove RH.

title: The L-function program generalized local factorization faster than global analytic realization
claim: Riemann's Euler product gives an exact bridge between prime-local factors and a global Dirichlet series on their common convergence domain. Later programs preserve that local-to-global interface across arithmetic and automorphic objects, and newform decomposition isolates primitive components with normalized Euler products and functional equations. But a universal package of local parameters and contragredient symmetry still leaves the separate burden of constructing and analytically continuing the global function.
historical_or_program_relation: The program expands from one proved dual representation to a family-wide architecture, while the historical bottleneck shifts toward global existence, meromorphic continuation, and justified completion rather than merely specifying local factors.
limits: A newspace dimension formula does not construct its basis or prove L-function factorization, and the automorphic package in the indexed unit is conjectural rather than an analytic realization theorem.

title: Finite-dimensional optimization helps only after analytic admissibility is compiled into the objective
claim: Two modern analytic programs turn infinite arithmetic inequalities into finite coefficient searches: enriched divisor weights reduce to explicit integral functionals for a gap criterion, while nonnegative trigonometric polynomials carry aggregate sign constraints for zero-free regions and are explored by annealing. In both, computation proposes a witness only after the analytic reduction fixes admissibility and the exact objective; proof still requires a certified global sign condition and a strict evaluated margin.
historical_or_program_relation: Auxiliary-function design evolves from hand-chosen features to systematic finite-dimensional search, but the mathematical advance is the prior compilation of arithmetic structure into checkable constraints, not the optimizer by itself.
limits: The two objectives address different theorems and are not transferable; higher degree need not improve the bound, heuristic annealing gives no global optimum, and a coefficient table alone does not certify nonnegativity or the final inequality.

title: Some zero-free advances hinge on crossing a narrow threshold rather than proving a full asymptotic
claim: The exceptional-zero and zero-free-region programs expose sharply localized bottlenecks. A fixed saving in a sieve constant would qualitatively repel an exceptional zero, while an iterative zero-free envelope needs exclusion only in explicit rectangles between successive profiles. Comparing reciprocal boundary functions also shows why an asymptotically better region may fail to dominate at finite height: the missing advance can be a threshold or local oracle, not wholesale control everywhere.
historical_or_program_relation: Later formulations increasingly express failure as a bounded interface obligation—a constant saving, a finite-height crossover, or a sequence of rectangle exclusions—so proof effort can target the exact point where propagation becomes available.
limits: The sieve implication and the iterative envelope concern different L-function settings and do not imply each other; the indexed units supply neither the constant improvement nor the missing rectangle-exclusion oracle.

title: Verified zero ranges became modular proof inputs only with provenance and dependency control
claim: A finite zero verification can outlive its original computation when it is preserved as a provenance-rich certificate and exposed through a scalar height parameter. Historical use in weak Goldbach and later proposed transfers to explicit prime estimates show the benefit, but also reveal that the certificate is only one typed input among analytic estimates, zero-free constants, and separate finite checks; the downstream interface must be proved rather than inferred from a larger number of verified zeros.
historical_or_program_relation: Computational RH work develops from reporting scale to producing reusable bounded evidence whose software, range, and proof dependencies can be audited by later analytic arguments.
limits: Finite L-function verification is not a global RH result, the Goldbach span does not specify the full interface to the circle method, and increasing H alone does not instantiate revised reciprocal-zeta or zero-density constants.
